sections.heading: SimplePractice vs Jane App vs TherapyNotes: Overview
sections.content: This comparison features three leading practice management platforms with distinct geographic and specialty strengths. SimplePractice is the US market leader serving 250,000+ practitioners with a comprehensive feature set. Jane App was built in Canada and excels for Canadian practices needing native Canadian billing (TELUS Health integration) and multi-disciplinary clinics. TherapyNotes was created specifically for behavioral health by a clinical psychologist and is US-only. Your choice depends heavily on your location, specialty mix, and whether you need e-prescribing.

sections.heading: Geographic Considerations: US vs Canada
sections.content: If you practice in Canada, Jane App is the clear choice. Built in North Vancouver, Jane offers native TELUS Health integration for Canadian insurance billing, PIPEDA and PHIPA (Ontario) compliance, and pricing in CAD. TherapyNotes is US-only and doesn't support Canadian billing workflows. SimplePractice serves US practices primarily, though Canadian users can use it with limitations. For US practices, all three work well, but SimplePractice and TherapyNotes have deeper US insurance billing integrations.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Pricing is relatively similar across all three platforms. SimplePractice ranges from $49-99/month. Jane App ranges from $54-99/month (with a low-appointment Balance tier at $54). TherapyNotes charges $69/month solo or $79+$50/additional for groups. Key differences: Jane App charges $20/month extra for US insurance billing, while SimplePractice and TherapyNotes include it. Jane's AI Scribe is cheapest at $15/month versus $35-40 for the others. TherapyNotes has the lowest per-claim cost at $0.14 versus SimplePractice's $0.25.

sections.heading: Specialty Focus
sections.content: TherapyNotes is the only platform built specifically for behavioral health, with note templates designed by a clinical psychologist. Jane App was originally designed for allied health (physiotherapy, chiropractic, massage) and later expanded to mental health, making it ideal for multi-disciplinary clinics with diverse provider types. SimplePractice serves the broadest audience including mental health, nutrition, and wellness. If your practice is exclusively mental health, TherapyNotes' purpose-built approach may offer advantages. If you run a multi-disciplinary clinic, Jane App excels.

sections.heading: Key Feature Differences
sections.content: SimplePractice is the only platform with e-prescribing (via DrFirst, $49/month), making it essential for prescribing providers. Jane App won a 2026 Silver Stevie Award for customer service excellence. TherapyNotes offers 24/7 phone and email support on all plans with free data import assistance. All three offer AI documentation assistants, with Jane's being the most affordable at $15/month. Jane App uniquely offers a website builder add-on ($59/month) for practices needing a web presence.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Match the platform to your specific situation:

recommendations.when: You're a US-based practice needing e-prescribing, you want the most feature-rich all-in-one platform, you serve wellness clients beyond mental health, you need extensive calendar integrations (Google, Apple, Outlook), or you prefer the largest user community

You practice in Canada and need native Canadian billing (TELUS Health), you run a multi-disciplinary clinic with various provider types, you prioritize exceptional customer service, you want the most affordable AI scribe ($15/month), or you need PIPEDA/PHIPA compliance

You want a platform built specifically for behavioral health, you need 24/7 phone support, you want the cheapest insurance claims ($0.14 each), you appreciate clinical templates designed by clinicians, or you prefer a bootstrapped company focused solely on mental health

faqs.q: Which is best for Canadian therapists: SimplePractice, Jane App, or TherapyNotes?
faqs.a: Jane App is the clear choice for Canadian therapists. Built in Canada, it offers native TELUS Health integration for Canadian insurance billing, PIPEDA and PHIPA compliance, and CAD pricing. TherapyNotes is US-only. SimplePractice can work for Canadian users but lacks native Canadian billing.

faqs.q: Which platform has e-prescribing for psychiatrists?
faqs.a: Only SimplePractice offers e-prescribing through DrFirst integration ($49/month plus $89 setup). Neither Jane App nor TherapyNotes currently offer e-prescribing. Prescribing providers should strongly consider SimplePractice for this capability.

faqs.q: Which has the best customer support?
faqs.a: TherapyNotes offers 24/7 phone and email support on all plans. Jane App won a 2026 Silver Stevie Award for customer service. SimplePractice has more limited support hours. For around-the-clock assistance, TherapyNotes leads; for award-winning service quality, Jane App excels.

faqs.q: Which is best for multi-disciplinary clinics?
faqs.a: Jane App was designed for multi-disciplinary practices and supports physiotherapy, chiropractic, massage, mental health, and more in one platform. SimplePractice also handles multiple specialties well. TherapyNotes is specifically designed for behavioral health and less suited for diverse provider types.

faqs.q: What are the AI documentation costs for each platform?
faqs.a: Jane App offers the cheapest AI Scribe at $15/month per practitioner. SimplePractice's AI Note Taker is $35/month. TherapyNotes' TherapyFuel AI is $40/clinician/month. All three offer AI-powered documentation to speed up note writing.

faqs.q: Which has the lowest insurance billing costs?
faqs.a: TherapyNotes has the lowest per-claim cost at $0.14 per claim. SimplePractice charges $0.25 per claim. Jane App requires a $20/month add-on for US insurance billing. For high-volume insurance billing, TherapyNotes offers the best value.
